editions.title: Yetsi'as Mitsrayim
editions.author: Moyshe Hurwitz
editions.notes: MS — 67 pp, 66 GT + 1 FINAL; Miriam Trinh primary editor. Text is in GERMAN (Latin script), not Yiddish — cf. sheet note "בדייטש". Title page: "Jezias Mizraim (Die Wunder von Egipten) / Biblische Operete in 4 Aufzügen / Von Profesor M. Horowitz, Musik von Perlmutter und Wohl"; Russian parallel title "Ециасъ Мицраимъ ... Соч. Професора М. Горовица. Музыка Перельмутера и Вола". expression.comments: Zylbercweig: "The role of Dr. Edvish was played by the author"; The play was written while Horowitz was in Romania, but was performed after his emigration to America at the Romanian Opera House. Acc. Z: B. Gorin wrote about this: "This was the one and only play on the Yiddish stage that was accompanied by a serialized talk that was not scripted. [...] In "Tisa Eslar" Horowitz wanted to create a great sensation, a drama that would grab everyone’s attention. The libel of Tisa Eslar at that time was fresh in the minds of everyone. Every Jew was interested in this libel. This was a true-to-life issue. The success of this play showed him that with such material it was possible to interest the public. So that when a national catastrophe, or a national misfortune arose, he took advantage of it to stage a drama." Done in daytshmerish.
